points.label: Normal-noise feedback tap

effects.title: Left and right reverse

points.label: Left report input

effects.title: DMC smaller decoding steps
effects.description: Use +/-1 instead of +/-2 per decoded bit. Changes sample shape and level excursion without changing playback rate. Audible only while the game uses DMC sampled audio; pulse/triangle/noise synthesis is unaffected directly.

points.label: DMC upward step
points.evidence: DeltaModulationChannel::Run at RVA 0x40AB00, directly called from NesApu::Run. Exact source matches reverse-bit-order selection, bit test, bounded +/-2 output update, then bit counter and DMA bookkeeping. Only the listed decoder operations change. Level guards stay <=125 for upward and >=2 for downward operations; all replacement arithmetic maps valid levels into 0..127. Sample addressing, timer, buffer refill, DMA and interrupt code are untouched.

effects.title: Pulse 1 fast fades
effects.description: Subtract four from this envelope divider per tick instead of one. Shortens automatic fades and accelerates looping envelopes. Fixed-volume passages may be unchanged.

points.label: Envelope divider speed
points.evidence: NesApu::FrameCounterTick at 0x19D6F0 matches source order pulse1, pulse2, triangle linear counter, noise, followed by the half-frame length/sweep section. ApuEnvelope fields at channel+0x21/22/23/24 hold volume, start, signed divider, counter. Normal counter is 0..15; divider reload is volume 0..15. Only the described envelope operation changes; channel length counters and frame-clock frequency are untouched. A valid 0..15 divider becomes -4..11; negative values immediately reload from volume. Counter decrement remains guarded above zero.

effects.description: Pulse channels use the decay counter where the game requested fixed volume, and fixed volume where it requested the decay counter. Can turn steady notes into fades or remove existing fades.

points.label: Pulse volume source

effects.title: Noise volume modes exchange

points.label: Noise volume source

effects.title: Short envelope cycles
effects.description: Pulse and noise envelope resets/loops start at 7 instead of 15. Reduces the peak and shortens the decay cycle. Audible when the decay counter supplies volume.

effects.title: Frozen fades
effects.description: Hold pulse/noise decay counters between resets instead of decreasing them. Notes still stop when the original channel length or mute rules require it. Fixed-volume output is unaffected.

points.label: Envelope decrement destination
points.evidence: NesApu::FrameCounterTick at 0x19D6F0 matches source order pulse1, pulse2, triangle linear counter, noise, followed by the half-frame length/sweep section. ApuEnvelope fields at channel+0x21/22/23/24 hold volume, start, signed divider, counter. Normal counter is 0..15; divider reload is volume 0..15. Only the described envelope operation changes; channel length counters and frame-clock frequency are untouched. DEC AL becomes DEC AH. AL still contains the unchanged bounded envelope counter and is stored as before. AH is dead after this point: later channel processing reloads EAX, and the method returns void. DEC flags are not consumed before the next CMP. This preserves AL without a multi-byte instruction rewrite.

effects.title: low bitplane offset
effects.description: Sample one background plane at a one-bit offset. Splits tile color detail without changing ROM data. Can change sprite-zero-hit timing and break games that depend on it. Restoring code does not undo gameplay.

points.label: Background bitplane sampling
points.evidence: DefaultNesPpu::Run inlined GetPixelColor. Shifted words are masked to bits 0/1 before OR; result stays 0..3. Also feeds sprite-zero-hit detection; gameplay compatibility is not assured.

effects.description: Permute pixels within horizontally mirrored sprite rows; both planes move together. Sprite positions and pattern fetch addresses stay unchanged. Unmirrored sprites are unaffected. Can alter sprite-zero hits.

points.label: Mirrored sprite row permutation

effects.title: Pulse 1 four-step melody
effects.description: Restrict this pulse sequencer to 3,2,1,0. Halves its sequence period and changes duty shape. Some duty/lookup combinations become constant or silent; game tempo and channel timers are unchanged.

points.label: Four-step pulse sequence
points.evidence: Original DEC AL followed by AND AL,7. Mask3 bounds every input byte to0..3, inside the original phase table. Changes no loop exit or timing arithmetic.

effects.title: Pulse 2 four-step melody
effects.description: Restrict this pulse sequencer to 3,2,1,0. Halves its sequence period and changes duty shape. Some duty/lookup combinations become constant or silent; game tempo and channel timers are unchanged.

points.label: Four-step pulse sequence
points.evidence: Original DEC AL followed by AND AL,7. Mask3 bounds every input byte to0..3, inside the original phase table. Changes no loop exit or timing arithmetic.

effects.title: Four-step triangle bass
effects.description: Cycle through the first four triangle samples rather than 32. Shortens the sequence and reduces its level excursion; can sound thinner or quieter, not necessarily louder. Timers and game tempo are unchanged.

points.label: Four-step triangle wrap
points.evidence: Original INC DL followed by AND DL,31. Mask3 bounds all states to0..3 in the original waveform table.

effects.title: Long repeating percussion
effects.description: Use noise feedback tap 2 in both noise modes. The seed-1 sequence repeats after 4599 steps, between the short repeating patterns and original long noise. Other starting states can have different periods; audible difference depends on the game.

points.label: Normal-noise feedback tap
points.evidence: Original 15-bit feedback recurrence; only the tap changes. No address, timer, width or loop-exit change.

points.label: Short-noise feedback tap
points.evidence: Same tap2 selected for short mode. Feedback remains bit0 XOR bit2, inserted at bit14.

effects.title: A and Down exchange
effects.description: Physical Down becomes A; physical A becomes Down. Other report bits remain unchanged. Changes can affect both standard controllers.

points.label: A report source
points.evidence: Standard NES ToByte report constructor. Only IsPressed button-ID immediate changes; same 0..7 physical button domain. Start/Select and controller serial shifting unchanged.

points.label: Down report source
points.evidence: Standard NES ToByte report constructor. Only IsPressed button-ID immediate changes; same 0..7 physical button domain. Start/Select and controller serial shifting unchanged.

effects.title: Vertical movement also presses A/B
effects.description: Physical Up produces Up+A; physical Down produces Down+B. Physical A/B no longer drive those two action bits. Start and Select stay unchanged. Can change movement, jumping and attacks depending on the game.
